transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, uh, I hope I'm not taking up time from people who really need it. I'm mostly just here because... well, I've been having a little bit of trouble with my focus lately. Nothing terrible, really! I'm still getting my routes done. 

It's just that out on the road—I drive a truck for a living—over these last few months, my mind just keeps jumping around. Like, every time the CB radio chirps, or I see a fuel price sign, or even just when I get a new idea in my head, I get completely sidetracked. And, well, it's a little embarrassing to admit because I pride myself on doing a good job, but I've been missing some details I normally never miss. Just silly mistakes, like overlooking a client's delivery note or forgetting who I promised to call back. 

I'm usually really on top of that stuff, I swear. I just wanted to check in and see if maybe I'm just stressed or something. I hope it's okay that I came in for that... does that make sense to you?
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about anything lately?

Anxious? Um, no, I wouldn't really say so. I mean, I hope that's okay to say—I definitely don't want to sound like I'm brushing off your question! It's just... I haven't really been worried about much lately. 

I've got a steady job, and I try to just take things as they come, you know? I mean, sure, there's always regular everyday stuff, but nothing that makes me feel nervous or on edge. I try to keep a pretty positive attitude about it all, so I wouldn't say anxiety is an issue for me. Is... is that a normal way to feel with what I was describing before? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had difficulty sustaining attention on tasks or activities even when you're not being distracted by something else?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. If it's quiet and there's nothing else going on around me, I can usually stick to what I'm doing just fine. I really do try my absolute best to stay focused, you know? 

It's mostly just... well, like I mentioned before, if something catches my eye or I get a sudden thought, that's when I kind of drift off. But if there are no distractions at all? No, my attention is actually pretty steady then. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just really don't want you to think I'm totally incapable out there on the road or anything, because I really do take pride in doing a good job. Did I answer that right for you?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Restless... well, um, I wouldn't really use the word fidgety. I hope it's okay to say that! I just... I like to be helpful, you know? It is true that I get a little antsy if I have to sit still for too long. But I really try to turn that into a positive! 

Lately, I just keep finding extra jobs for myself to do. Like, I'll spend my time rewriting my route plans to make them more efficient, or I'll call up the new drivers after hours just to check on them and make sure they're doing alright. And even at home, I'm always finding little things to fix around the house. 

I figure it's good to be a hard worker, right? I just like being productive rather than sitting around doing nothing. I hope that's not a bad thing... does that answer your question okay?
Do you often find yourself having trouble organizing your thoughts or expressing them in a coherent manner?

Organizing my thoughts? Um, no, I don't think I have any trouble with that. I mean, I hope I'm making sense right now! I always try to be as clear as possible when I talk to people. 

Sometimes I guess I might jump from one idea to another, but that's just because I have so many good ideas lately, you know? Like with the route planning and helping the new guys. I just get excited to share what I'm thinking about. But I can always explain myself if someone asks me to slow down. 

I really try to make sure people understand me. Am I making sense to you? I just want to be sure I'm giving you a clear picture of everything.
Are your difficulties with focus and getting sidetracked causing problems for you at work or in your relationships with others?

Well, um... I really hope it's not causing too many problems. I mean, I always try my hardest to do a good job, you know? But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest—and I want to be honest with you—there have been a few little hiccups. 

At work, sometimes I've had to ask dispatch or the clients to repeat some details that... well, I probably should have caught the first time. And, um, a couple of my sales follow-ups might have slipped through the cracks. Just because I had so many other great ideas I was chasing all at once! I really didn't mean to drop the ball, I promise. I just got a little overly eager to help.

And at home... well, I've noticed my wife and daughter have been acting a little quiet around me. Kind of walking on eggshells, I guess. I can tell I might be adding a little bit of strain, even though I'm really just trying to help fix things up around the house and be a good provider. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or a bad husband. I really do mean well. Is it normal to have a few slip-ups like that when you're trying to do so much?
Have you noticed any changes in how your family or friends interact with you since you started having these focus issues?

Yeah, um, like I was just mentioning a second ago... I really have noticed it mostly with my wife and daughter. They’ve been, you know, kind of walking on eggshells around me lately. I can just feel that I’m adding a bit of strain to the house, which is the exact opposite of what I want! I’m supposed to be helping them and making things easier, not stressing them out. I really hope I'm not being a burden on them... do you think they know I mean well? 

And I guess it’s kind of the same thing at work with how people are interacting with me. Like I said, having to ask dispatch or my clients to repeat details I really should have tracked the first time... it makes me feel like I'm letting them down. Plus those couple of sales follow-ups that slipped through because I was chasing too many ideas at once... I just really hate the thought that people might be frustrated with me. I always try to be a good, reliable guy for everybody. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much. Am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions.
Have you had to cut back on any work or social activities because of your difficulty with focus and getting sidetracked?

Oh, no, definitely not. I haven't cut back on anything. I really pride myself on being a hard worker, you know? I would hate to call out of a route or cancel on my family just because my mind is wandering a little bit. 

If anything, I just try to push through it and work even harder to make up for those little slip-ups I told you about. I figure it's always better to just keep showing up and doing my best, rather than stepping back. I really hope that's the right way to handle it? I just don't want anyone—especially you or my boss—to think I'm slacking off or giving up. I'm still giving it a hundred and ten percent!
Have you experienced any significant problems at work or in your personal relationships as a result of your difficulties with focus and getting sidetracked?

Well, um... I know I've kind of touched on this already, and I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record here. I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

Like I mentioned, I wouldn't call them *significant* problems. Just little bumps in the road, really. At work, yeah, I've had to ask dispatch and a few clients to repeat some details that I probably should have caught the first time around. And, um, a couple of my sales follow-ups did slip through the cracks just because my brain was going in a million different directions with all these great ideas. But I'm still trying my absolute hardest, I promise. 

And at home... well, like I said, my wife and daughter have been sort of walking on eggshells around me. I can definitely tell I'm adding a bit of strain to the house right now, which makes me feel awful because I'm supposed to be the one helping them and keeping things running smooth. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible guy. I mean, everybody drops the ball sometimes when they're trying to do too much, right? Do you think that's pretty normal?
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I really try my best to be a good listener. I mean, in my line of work, you know, dealing with clients on the route, you really have to let the other person finish. It's just good manners, right? 

I would feel absolutely terrible if I was cutting people off or being rude. Sometimes, sure, my mind is going a little fast with all those ideas I mentioned earlier, but I always try to just... bite my tongue and wait my turn. 

I hope I haven't interrupted you at all today? I really want to make sure I'm being respectful of your time and giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you often find yourself talking more than others in social situations?

Well, um, I don't really think so. I mean, I try to be pretty aware of how much I'm talking. Like I said, I really value being a good listener, especially with my clients and my family. 

I guess sometimes, when I get really excited about a new idea or a project, I might get a little... enthusiastic? And maybe I talk a bit more than usual just because I want to share it with everyone. But I wouldn't say I dominate the conversation or anything like that. I always try to make sure other people get a chance to chime in. 

I really hope I'm not coming across as someone who just talks someone's ear off. I've been doing okay with that today, right? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need without rambling too much.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your overall performance or relationships due to your difficulties with focus and getting sidetracked?

Well, um... I know we sort of touched on this a little bit earlier, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture here. 

Like I mentioned before, I wouldn't call them, you know, *significant* changes. Just some minor hiccups. At work, yeah, I've had to ask dispatch or a couple of the clients on my route to repeat some details that I probably should have caught the first time. And maybe a couple of my sales follow-ups slipped through the cracks just because I was chasing so many different ideas at once. But I'm still getting the job done, I promise. I'm really trying my best to stay on top of it.

And at home... well, it's just like I said, my wife and daughter have been kind of walking on eggshells around me lately. I can definitely tell I'm adding a bit of strain to the house right now, which is the last thing I want to do. I'm supposed to be the one helping them out, you know? 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm failing at everything. I mean, it's pretty normal to drop the ball a little when you've got a lot going on, right? I'm doing okay, aren't I?
Do you often blurting out answers before questions have been completed?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try to wait until someone is completely done talking before I say anything. Like I was saying about being a good listener, I think it's just so important to let people finish their thoughts. 

Sometimes, if I'm pretty sure I know what they're going to ask, especially on the route when a customer is asking about a delivery time or something standard, I might, you know, just nod and agree before they get the whole sentence out. Just to show I'm following along and to save them time, really. But I don't just blurt things out or talk over them. 

I'd hate for anyone to think I was being impatient or dismissive. I try really hard to be polite. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering these questions the way you need me to.
Do you often act on impulse without much consideration for the consequences?

Well, um, no, not really. I mean, I try to be pretty thoughtful about what I do. I wouldn't say I'm impulsive. 

I guess sometimes, you know, if I get a really great idea for a new sales approach or maybe I see something nice I want to pick up for my wife or daughter, I might just go for it. But it's always with good intentions, you know? I just want to make things better or make them happy. I wouldn't say I just do things without thinking about what might happen. I always try to keep my responsibilities in mind. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound reckless or anything. I try to be a responsible guy. I'm doing okay, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about how I handle things.
Do you often feel like you're 'on the go' or like you're 'driven by a motor'?

Well, um... driven by a motor makes it sound kind of extreme, I guess. I wouldn't really put it exactly like that. I just... well, I like to stay busy. Being a hard worker is a good thing, right? 

I have been finding a few extra jobs for myself lately, just to help out where I can. Like, I'll sit down and rewrite some of our route plans to make them a bit more efficient, or I might check in on a couple of the new drivers after hours, just to make sure they're getting the hang of things. And then at home, I've been fixing up a few little things around the house that have been on the back burner. 

I guess I do get a little bit antsy if I sit still for too long right now. I just prefer being useful instead of sitting around doing nothing. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm out of control or anything. It's pretty normal to just want to get things done and help people out, isn't it? I'm doing alright?
Did you have any difficulties with behavior or paying attention when you were a child?

Oh, no, I was a pretty good kid. I mean, my mom always said I was a handful, but you know how boys are, right? Just full of energy and wanting to be outside playing instead of sitting at a desk. 

I never really got into any major trouble at school or anything. I tried to pay attention, I really did. Sometimes I'd get a little distracted if a subject wasn't my favorite, but I always managed to get my work done and pass my classes. I think I was just a normal kid who liked to have fun. 

I wouldn't say I had any real difficulties, just the usual growing pains. I hope that's what you're asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I was back then.
Did your parents or teachers ever express concerns about your behavior or attention span when you were growing up?

Well, um, no, not that I can remember. I mean, like I said, my mom thought I had a lot of energy, but she never seemed worried about it. She just thought I was an active boy. 

And my teachers, they never really pulled my parents aside or sent notes home saying I was a problem. I might have gotten a "needs to talk less in class" on a report card once or twice, but that's pretty standard, right? Just kids being kids. Nobody ever made a big deal out of it or thought something was wrong with me. 

I was always respectful to my teachers, and I tried my best. That's the most important thing, isn't it? I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I was a bad kid or anything. I was just a regular guy growing up. Does that make sense?
Have you experienced difficulties with focus and getting sidetracked for most of your life?

Well, gosh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, with my line of work—driving the routes and making all those stops—you really have to stay sharp, you know? You can't just be getting sidetracked when you're behind the wheel of a truck all day. So I've always made sure to keep my eyes on the road and focus on the task at hand. 

I mean, sure, maybe if it's been a really long shift and I'm tired, my mind might wander for just a second, but that happens to everybody, right? It's nothing that ever stopped me from doing a good job or anything like that. I've always prided myself on being a reliable guy who pays attention. 

I don't think I have any real problems with focus. I'm answering these questions okay, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know, and I hope I'm not coming across like I'm scatterbrained or anything.
Do you often feel an internal restlessness or an urge to be constantly moving?

Well, um, I wouldn't call it restlessness, exactly. I mean, I just like to stay productive, you know? It's a good thing to be a hard worker, right? 

Lately, I've just been... well, I keep finding extra jobs for myself. Like, I'll spend my evenings rewriting my route plans to make them more efficient, or I'll check in on the new drivers after hours just to make sure they're doing okay. And then when I get home, I'm always fixing things around the house. 

I guess I do feel a little, I don't know, antsy if I just sit still on the couch for too long. But that's just because I want to be helpful and get things done. It's better to be active than lazy, don't you think? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything, I'm just trying to be a good provider and employee. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Did you experience any difficulties with focus, attention, or impulsivity as a child that have continued into adulthood?

Well, um, no, not really. I mean, I think we talked about this a little bit already, right? I was just a regular kid. I didn't have any real trouble paying attention in school, and I certainly wasn't impulsive or getting into trouble. 

And as an adult, like I said, I've always been pretty focused, especially with driving. You have to be. I've always just tried to do the right thing and be responsible. I've never been the type to just do things without thinking or let my mind wander when I'm supposed to be working. 

I really hope I'm answering this right. I just don't want you to think I've had these lifelong problems or that I'm not a capable person. I'm doing okay with these questions, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of who I am.
